title: Task-aware metric orchestrator for quant profile validation and gating
creator: Leah Martinez
description: Implement a reusable, task-aware metric orchestrator that runs against FP8/INT8 quantization profiles during calibration and produces gating decisions for rollout. The orchestrator will standardize metric contracts, execute a battery of scores (perplexity, MMLU-style accuracy, ROUGE/BLEU, and specialized task scorers), aggregate results into a pass/fail policy, and emit artifacts consumed by the release pipeline and Console QA dashboards.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Orchestrator runs end-to-end for a given quant_profile and model_version, producing a JSON report stored in s3 and indexed in the eval DB.

2) Implemented metric adapters for: perplexity (causal LM token-perplexity), MMLU-style multiple-choice accuracy harness, ROUGE and BLEU for summarization/translation tasks, and two example task-specific scorers (QA F1 and semantic-rerank NDCG).
3) Defined metric thresholds and degradation budgets in a policy file (e.g., max absolute MMLU drop <= 1.5%, perplexity increase <= 5%, ROUGE/BLUE drop <= 2).
4) Orchestrator produces a deterministic gate decision: PASS | SOFT_FAIL | FAIL with rationale and link to artifacts.

5) Integration hooks: (a) runtime rollout can automatically fallback to a higher-precision variant when gate returns FAIL; (b) Console dashboard ingests metric time-series and exposes regression alerts.
6) Unit and integration tests covering adapters and aggregation logic with synthetic fixtures included in the repo.
implementation_notes: Architecture: lightweight coordinator service that calls existing evaluation harness workers. Coordinator accepts a profile descriptor (model, quant_profile, dataset_set), dispatches tasks to adapters, collects metrics, and runs aggregation rules.

Metric contracts: each adapter must return a flat dictionary: {metric_name: float, direction: "higher_is_better"|"lower_is_better", confidence_interval: float, samples: int}. We'll define this contract in docs/metric_contract.md and validate at runtime.

Datasets: use curated evaluation buckets: mmluv2_rc (mcq), summarization_goldset_v2, wmt-translation-subsample, qa-dev-f1. Datasets are referenced by stable id and snapshot hash to ensure reproducibility.
Calibration coupling: orchestrator will accept calibration artifacts (scale tables, per-layer min/max, sample selection) and re-run targeted evals for layers flagged as brittle.
Performance: orchestration should parallelize adapter runs and stream results; large suites must support partial-result publishing so rollouts can inspect early failures.
- aggregate: any FAIL -> FAIL; if no FAILs and >=2 SOFT_FAILs -> SOFT_FAIL; otherwise PASS.
Fallback actions: if FAIL -> annotate profile with failed_metrics and trigger rebuild with relaxed quant_bins or per-tensor fallback to INT16 for flagged layers.

Observability: each run emits metrics to Prometheus + persisted JSON to S3 under s3://redwood-evals/quant_profiles/{profile}/{run_id}/report.json and creates a Console entry with links to raw outputs and diff visualizations.
test_plan: Unit tests for metric adapters (perplexity, mmlu, rouge, bleu, qa-f1, ndcg) using canned model outputs and golden labels.
Integration test: CI job that runs orchestrator on a tiny sample snapshot and verifies gating outcomes for two synthetic quant profiles (one expected PASS, one expected FAIL).
Load test: run orchestration with full MMLU and summarization subsets on a staging cluster to measure latency and parallelism scaling. Verify partial-report behavior under worker failures.
Regression test: create a nightly job that re-runs previous successful profiles and asserts that reported metrics remain within ±0.2% for deterministic seeds.
End-to-end: simulate runtime rollout where FAIL triggers automated fallback and ensure the customer route remains healthy (latency/SLO checks).
